clue.text: Dismiss objection to the instrument

parts.note: to dismiss an employee is to sack them
a 'but' is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Someone is told to drop their protest against a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is an early form of trombone, a brass wind instrument of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Sessions that welcome late arrivals

parts.note: late means dead, so these meetings receive spirits of the departed, not latecomers

explanation.surface: Meetings where people turning up late are made welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' looks like tardy; it means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritualist sittings aim to contact the dead, the departed being the late arrivals.

clue.text: Raft is able to span a river

indicators.note: to span is to stretch across, so the word for being able goes round the rest

parts.note: can means is able
the Tamar is the river between Devon and Cornwall

explanation.surface: A raft that can cross from bank to bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The TAMAR is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-hulled boat, loosely a raft of logs lashed together in its original Tamil form.

clue.text: Rush into the boat

explanation.surface: Someone hurries aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge in is to rush in rudely; a flat-bottomed canal vessel carries the same name.

clue.text: Dressing kit camouflages eastern stiletto

indicators.note: camouflage disguises, so the letters appear in a changed form

explanation.surface: A grooming case conceals an oriental dagger.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of brushes, combs and the like used when getting dressed and groomed.

clue.text: Moving images of favourite young dogs

explanation.surface: Photos or films of beloved puppies in motion.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two words: young dogs (pups) that are favourites (pets).
explanation.definitionFit: Marionettes are figures made to move by strings; split in two the word describes pups kept as pets.

clue.text: Bird seed has it

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed

explanation.surface: A bird has found some seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird such as the meadow or tree variety.

clue.text: Manuscript brings honour to men in part

indicators.note: in puts the honour and the men inside the word part

parts.note: taken as written
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award
taken as written

explanation.surface: A document grants an award to some men.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order.
explanation.definitionFit: Old documents were written on treated animal skin, the material standing for the writing.

clue.text: Order found in the dictionary

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the words the dictionary

explanation.surface: A command looked up in a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is a decree or official command.

clue.text: Element of burning interest to match-makers

definitions.text: Element of burning interest to match-makers

parts.words: Element of burning interest to match-makers
parts.note: match-makers here are makers of matches for striking, not romantic go-betweens; the element that burns on a match head

explanation.surface: Something that fascinates people who arrange marriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match-makers' suggests romance; it means makers of matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Brimstone, the yellow element, was used in match heads because it burns readily.

clue.text: Garrick, for instance, in the guise of Bill Hill

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Garrick appears disguised as someone called Bill Hill.
explanation.walkthrough: David Garrick was the great 18th-century London stage star.
explanation.definitionFit: David Garrick was a celebrated English stage performer, an example of a player of roles.

clue.text: Unbiased, I take part in mail distribution

indicators.note: in places the word part inside the shuffled letters
distribution spreads the letters of mail out into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fair-minded person helps with sorting the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' turns MAIL into MIAL, and 'in' puts PART inside it after the M; I goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unbiased is fair and takes no side.

clue.text: Qualified to contend, and not without love

parts.note: to contend is to compete

indicators.note: without tells us to drop the letter for love from the word not

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone eligible to enter a contest, provided they have love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes O (love, a zero score in tennis) out of NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualified person is capable and fit for the job.

clue.text: Brood of chickens on board

explanation.surface: Young chicks kept aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A brood is a set of chicks born at one time; a ship's deck opening found on board bears the same name.

clue.text: Cancel the fight

explanation.surface: An order to call off the bout.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel a plan is to drop it; a fight is a brawl or scuffle, the noun sense.

clue.text: Growth produced by Peter Neal, perhaps

indicators.note: produced by means the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Something grown by a man called Peter Neal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced by' rearranges PETER NEAL; 'perhaps' marks the answer as one example of growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree is a growing thing; the London plane is a common example.

clue.text: Give up on French return

parts.note: sur is French for on
to render is to give back, return

explanation.surface: Admitting defeat over a return to France.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up is to yield or capitulate.

clue.text: Noisy extortioner ?

parts.note: a racket is a din, so the word for a gangster running a scam reads as one who makes a racket

explanation.surface: A loud criminal demanding money.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster who extorts by threats; a racket is also a loud noise.

clue.text: Wild ruffian brandishes a rod with speed

indicators.note: to brandish is to wave about, so the letters are flung into a new order

explanation.surface: A thug waves a stick about quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperate, reckless outlaw is a wild ruffian.

clue.text: Fanciful description of Diaghilev's toyshop

explanation.surface: A whimsical account of the toyshop in a Russian ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: Diaghilev's Ballets Russes staged La Boutique fantasque, known in English by this adjective plus 'Toyshop'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanciful means imaginative or unreal; the ballet title describes its toyshop with the same word.

clue.text: Lets go one article to Iris's S. African relation

parts.note: to let go is to free
I is the Roman numeral one
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone releases an item to a South African relative of Iris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' looks like a woman's name; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This fragrant flower from southern Africa belongs to the iris family.

clue.text: Jobs to request in a back street

indicators.note: in places the request inside the turned street letters
back says the abbreviation for street is read the other way

parts.note: to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Errands involving asking for things in a side street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ST into TS, and 'in' puts ASK inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Jobs are pieces of work, duties assigned.

clue.text: The Spanish gentleman at the centre is a politician

indicators.note: at the centre puts the word at in the middle of the Spanish title

parts.note: señor is the Spanish for a gentleman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman at the heart of things is in politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a legislature such as the US Senate is a politician.

clue.text: Follow directions to take to court

parts.note: E and N are two compass directions, east and north
to sue is to take legal action against

explanation.surface: Instructions to bring a lawsuit are carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow is to come after as a result, the sense of result.

clue.text: Positions spectacles, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word spoken aloud gives the entry

parts.note: sights are spectacles, things worth seeing

explanation.surface: Someone places glasses, so we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: Sites are locations or places.

clue.text: Ivy is always on the go!

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'for ever'
a green traffic light means go

explanation.surface: Ivy as a restless person who never stops moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ivy' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, which keeps its leaves all year.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy keeps its leaves through winter, an example of a plant that never goes bare.

clue.text: Banish to a former French island

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
île is French for island

explanation.surface: Sending someone away to an island once ruled by France.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile is to send someone away from their homeland.

clue.text: Note the downfall of the crop

parts.note: G is a musical note
rain is a downfall, falling water

explanation.surface: Observe the collapse of the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat and other cereals harvested are grain.

clue.text: Leaden variety of urn in east

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so these letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dull grey kind of urn found in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden here means gloomy and heavy; in old lore lead is the metal of the planet Saturn.

clue.text: A great cry of "Stop"

parts.note: vast means great in size

explanation.surface: A loud shout telling someone to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the sailor's call to cease or hold fast.

clue.text: Severely simple article to use about three times

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about means the word use goes round the Latin term

parts.note: taken as written
ter is Latin for three times, used in prescriptions

explanation.surface: A plain item to be used around three times.
explanation.walkthrough: TER, Latin for three times, sits inside USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means plain and without ornament, strict in style.

clue.text: Bitterness of a private soldier, say

indicators.note: say signals that a word spoken aloud gives the entry

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks, not an officer

explanation.surface: The resentment felt by an ordinary infantryman.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated resentment or ill will.
